questions.q: Farm animals used primarily to carry heavy loads and pull implements on the farm are called ________.
questions.explain: Work animals, also known as draught animals (such as oxen, donkeys, and camels), are reared for pulling ploughs, carts, and carrying heavy farm produce.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Which of the following farm animals is primarily reared for the production of milk?
questions.explain: Dairy cattle are specifically bred and raised for the ability to produce large quantities of milk.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Which animal is commonly kept on farms primarily to protect livestock and farm property from predators and thieves?
questions.explain: Dogs are the most common guard animals used on farms to secure livestock, equipment, and premises against intruders or wild predators.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Domesticated birds raised by humans for their meat and eggs are collectively referred to as ________.
questions.explain: Poultry refers to domesticated birds such as chickens, turkeys, ducks, and geese raised commercially or domestically for meat, eggs, and feathers.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Animals kept at home for pleasure, companionship, and amusement rather than for utility or meat are called ________.
questions.explain: Pets (like cats and parrots) are kept strictly for companionship and psychological benefits, not as food or work animals.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Fishes, crabs, and shrimps are classified based on their natural habitat as ________.
questions.explain: Aquatic animals are those that live in water. Fish, crabs, and shrimps dwell in aquatic habitats like ponds, rivers, and oceans.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Which of the following characteristics is unique to farm animals classified as mammals?
options: They have feathers covering their bodies
They give birth to young alive and produce milk
questions.explain: Mammals give birth to live young ones (viviparous) and have mammary glands which they use to suckle their young with milk.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Based on stomach type, cattle, sheep, and goats are classified as ruminants because they possess a ________.
questions.explain: Ruminants are animals that chew the cud and have a complex stomach divided into four compartments (rumen, reticulum, omasum, and abomasum).
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Which of the following farm animals is an example of a non-ruminant (monogastric) animal?
questions.explain: Pigs are non-ruminants because they have a simple, single-chambered stomach (monogastric system), unlike cattle, sheep, and goats which are ruminants.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Based on size classification, which of the following is considered a 'macro' (large) farm animal?
questions.explain: Horses, cattle, and camels fall under large farm animals due to their massive body sizes and weights, while poultry and rabbits are micro or small farm animals.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Which of the following farm animals is primarily classified as a non-mammal?
questions.explain: A turkey is a bird (avian), hence it is a non-mammalian farm animal. Pigs, rabbits, and goats are mammals.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: In agriculture, the processed skin of cattle and sheep is economically important because it is used for the production of ________.
questions.explain: Hides (from large animals) and skins (from small animals) are tanned and processed into leather for making shoes, bags, and belts.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Cattle raised specifically to provide meat for human consumption are referred to as ________.
questions.explain: Beef cattle are bred and raised extensively for meat production, whereas dairy cattle are raised for milk.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Which part of a poultry bird's digestive system performs the grinding of food, acting as a functional substitute for teeth?
questions.explain: Because birds lack teeth, they swallow grit and stones which are held in the gizzard. The muscular walls of the gizzard grind the feed into smaller particles.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Agriculture Fundamentals & Soil Science
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies
questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals

questions.q: Animal droppings (faeces) are highly beneficial on the farm as they are mainly used to ________.
questions.explain: Farm animal waste, such as cow dung and poultry droppings, is an excellent source of organic manure (farmyard manure) that improves soil fertility.
